Architecture

Kata has two halves. One is the application you build. The other is the tool that checks it. The checks build your binary and run it, so nothing reaches inside your code and your internal design is yours.

The fake server is a real HTTP server. It binds a socket, parses your request, checks your headers, and writes Server-Sent Events with real chunk boundaries. Only the content of the reply is scripted. That is the whole design: replace the model, keep the wire.

Repository layout

PathRole
agent/The agent you build. The only directory a learner edits.
starter/The initial state of agent/. Used to grade chapter 01 and by kata reset.
reference/chNN/Overlay of the files as they must be after chapter NN.
chapters/NN-slug/README.md, overview.md, problem.md, example.md, checks/.
internal/fake/Scripted OpenAI-compatible server. The far side of the seam.
internal/grader/Case DSL, bounded execution, report, diffs.
internal/hints/The three-rung hint ladder, keyed by chapter and case.
cmd/kata/The CLI: submit, read, hint, list, progress, verify, reset.
docs/Architecture, chapter format, writing style.

A submit run

A build error is reported as "not ready". It never counts as a failed case, because a learner who mistyped an import has not got the logic wrong.

How chapters relate

Chapters are cumulative. Chapter NN's code is a subset of chapter NN+1's. That property is what makes "your earlier chapters stay green" a guarantee instead of a hope.

The state before chapter NN is derived by applying reference/ch01 through reference/chNN-1. It is not stored, so it cannot drift.

kata verify grades every chapter twice: once against its after state, which must pass, and once against its before state, which must fail at least one case. A chapter whose starter passes grades nothing. A chapter whose reference fails cannot be completed. Both are caught offline.

The grading pipeline

Every case runs with a timeout and a panic barrier. A harness that blocks costs one case with its name attached, not the whole chapter.

The seams

The harness is built around six interfaces. Chapters 05 to 11 add implementations of them; they do not rewrite the loop.

InterfaceMethodImplemented by
ProviderChat(ctx, Request) (Message, Usage, error)chapter 01, extended in 02
ToolName, Description, Schema, Executechapter 03
ContributorContribute(ctx) (string, error), appended to the system promptchapter 05 (context files), 09 (skills)
TrimmerFit([]Message, budget) ([]Message, error)chapter 07
SteeringDrain() []Message, polled after each tool batchchapter 08
RecorderAppend(Event) error, Load(id) ([]Message, error)chapter 06
ToolSourceTools(ctx) ([]Tool, error), merged into the registrychapter 10 (subagent), 11 (MCP)

A change that makes a later chapter edit loop.go is a design error, not a scheduling problem. The seams exist so the course stays additive.

Two honest notes about these interfaces.

Production harnesses do not define most of them. pi and PiG use concrete session types, not a session interface. crush exposes services (session.Service, message.Service) rather than a registry. The interfaces here are teaching seams, chosen so that chapters stay additive and so that a check can substitute a scripted implementation. They are good design, not doctrine.

The provider seam is deliberately lossy. Chat returns one finished message, which hides the stream. That is the right compression for chapters 01 to 03. Chapter 04 refactors the same parser into a Stream call that reports deltas as they arrive, and keeps Chat as a thin collect-the-stream wrapper. Nothing about the wire changes; only what the caller can see while it arrives.

Where to read the real thing, by concern:

ConcernReadNot
the loop, event order, tool batchingPiG agent/agent_loop.gocrush, whose loop lives in charm.land/fantasy
permission policy as a first-class servicecrush internal/permission/pi or PiG, which expose hooks only
MCP over stdio, hand-rolledPiG/pi MCP clientscrush, which uses the official Go SDK

Grading policy

Two drivers, one rule. Grade the largest thing that can carry the claim.

Claim typeDriverWhy
"the program answers a prompt"black boxonly the process proves it is an application
"the program runs a tool and continues"black boxthe loop, the registry and the wire all participate
"the session resumes with prior turns"black boxneeds a real process, a real file, a second run
"the request stays under the budget"black boxinspect the third request the program sent
"this pure transform is correct"functionno process needed, and the diff is far more precise
"all 40 combinations of chunk boundaries"functionone process per split is 40 processes for no realism

Black box is the default. It is the only driver that can prove the thing you built runs, and it leaves the internal design free.

Function level is the exception, and it needs a pinned surface: a small exported function whose signature the chapter states up front. Two rules keep it honest:

  1. The pinned surface is the smallest possible type. If a []Message in and

[]Message out can express it, do not pin anything larger.

  1. A pinned function is a contract, not an architecture. The chapter says what

it must do, never how it is built.

A chapter that mixes the two declares both, case by case:

checks/ch07_test.go
  budget-ceiling      black box   run the program, inspect request 3
  budget-orphans      black box   inspect every request for unpaired calls
  estimate-tokens     function    EstimateTokens, pinned in agent/contract.go

Neither driver is allowed to weaken the other. A black-box case never asserts on a log line the program could fake, and a function case never stands in for a behaviour a user would notice.

Determinism

LayerFakedProves
Processnothing: your binary runs for realthe program works when invoked
TransportHTTP server speaking SSEyour wire code is correct
Behaviourscripted model decisionsyour loop, tools, and context logic
Outputfull request traces, per casenothing drifted silently

There is no layer that proves the agent is good. Quality needs a real model, money, and judgement. Kata grades correctness of the harness, and says so.

Adding a chapter

  1. chapters/NN-slug/checks/chNN_test.go with cases in the grader.Suite DSL.
  2. internal/hints/hints.go entries, three rungs each. The completeness test

fails if a case has no ladder or a ladder has no case.

  1. reference/chNN/ with only the files this chapter changes.
  2. overview.md, problem.md, example.md, README.md.
  3. kata verify. It must be clean before the chapter counts as written.

Glossary

TermMeaning
HarnessThe code around a model that turns text into actions: provider, tools, loop, state.
SeamAn interface you can replace. The provider seam is the one the grader uses.
Scripted modelA fixture that replays a fixed reply. Not a mock of your code.
CaseOne graded assertion with an id, a reason, and three hint rungs.
Before stateThe harness with chapters NN and later removed.
After stateThe harness with chapters 01 through NN applied.
